summary: Eight selected papers cover experimentally controllable net-charge fluctuation tests of thermal QCD, electromagnetic directed flow, neutron-skin geometry, ultra-peripheral GDR correlations, an ALICE anti-4Li search, transformer calorimeter reconstruction, ML-surrogate multiloop amplitudes, and particle-native neural operators.
professional_summary: The strongest heavy-ion contribution develops an acceptance-aware route from charge balance functions to lattice-QCD susceptibility tests. A validated electromagnetic hydrodynamic framework describes charge-odd directed flow but leaves conductivity extraction model dependent. The strongest ML contributions use a surrogate to enable a direct two-loop ttH calculation and introduce a mathematically controlled particle-native neural operator with broad kinetic-plasma validation.
strongest_paper_summary: An experimentally grounded route connects charge balance functions and multiplicity densities to net-charge cumulants needed for a lattice-QCD test of thermal equilibrium, with the decisive fourth-order extension still outstanding.

papers.title: Testing thermal equilibrium in heavy-ion collisions with electric-charge fluctuations
papers.abstract: Recent lattice-QCD electric-charge susceptibilities differ strongly from hadron-resonance-gas expectations, motivating measurements of net-charge cumulants. The paper expresses the second cumulant through the balance function and charged-particle density to make acceptance and efficiency effects experimentally tractable.

papers.title: Tracing Electromagnetic Response through Charge Splitting of Directed Flow in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
papers.short_authors: Ankit Kumar Panda, Zhu Meng, Long-Gang Pang, Xin-Nian Wang
papers.abstract: The observed beam-energy change in charge splitting of directed flow is modeled with viscous hydrodynamics coupled to electromagnetic fields and an electromagnetic Cooper-Frye correction. Electric and magnetic distortions compete, with their balance governed by effective conductivity; identified-particle predictions are provided.

papers.title: Disentangling the neutron skin of 48Ca from nuclear radius effects through 48Ca+48Ca and 48Ti+48Ti flow observables
papers.abstract: Transport simulations vary the 48Ca neutron skin and nuclear radius independently, comparing Ca-Ca with Ti-Ti at LHC energy. Flow-mean-pT covariance and its normalized correlation emerge as the most sensitive candidate observables.

papers.title: Quantum Correlations Between Two Giant Dipole Resonances in Ultra-Peripheral Collisions
papers.short_authors: Albandry Alshammri, Ashik Ikbal Sheikh, Declan Keane, Prithwish Tribedy, Gang Wang, Zhangbu Xu, Jie Zhao
papers.abstract: Three mechanisms for two-neutron azimuthal correlations in mutual GDR excitation are implemented in a Monte Carlo model. An assumed correlated phase yields a pronounced dipole only for small relative emission times, while averaging suppresses it.

papers.title: Search for anti-4Li from antiproton + anti-3He femtoscopy in Pb-Pb collisions at 5.36 TeV with ALICE
papers.short_authors: Giorgio Alberto Lucia (on behalf of the ALICE Collaboration)
papers.abstract: A femtoscopic search reconstructs anti-4Li through antiproton and anti-3He pairs in Pb-Pb collisions. The proposed yield comparison with anti-4He is intended to test nucleosynthesis models.

papers.title: End-to-end Particle Reconstruction with Transformers in High-Granularity Calorimeters
papers.short_authors: Qiming Bao, Haotian Bi, Benedikt Maier, Alex Tapper, Lauri Laatu
papers.abstract: Transformer models based on learned queries, diffusion, and flow matching reconstruct particles from simulated high-granularity calorimeter hits. They outperform the evaluated clustering baseline on recovery and energy resolution, with query and flow models retaining competitive throughput.

papers.title: Two-loop QCD contribution to quark-initiated top-antitop-Higgs production at the LHC
papers.short_authors: Xiang Chen, Massimiliano Grazzini, Stefan Kallweit
papers.abstract: Numerical multiloop methods and a learned phase-space surrogate enable a direct two-loop virtual ttH calculation in a leading-colour approximation. The result is consistent with prior approximate treatments and provides a route to practical cross-section integration.

papers.title: NEOPIC: A Neural Operator Framework for Particle-based Kinetic Plasma Simulations
papers.short_authors: Sriramkrishnan Muralikrishnan, Chelsea Maria John, Jeffrey Kelling, Michael Bussmann, Robert Speck, Paul Gibbon
papers.abstract: A nonuniform Fourier neural operator maps particle measures directly to fields and can replace the field solve in several particle-based kinetic methods. The work supplies convergence and complexity analysis plus multi-physics numerical validation in two and three dimensions.

cautions.reason: The phase-lock mechanism is assumed, the largest signal requires idealized emission-time selection, and detector-level/time-inclusive feasibility is not established.
Proceedings abstract reports the method and motivation but no quantitative yield, significance, uncertainty, or limit.
